methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $78M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
WeaveGrid is a Series B climate and energy technology company founded by Apoorv Bhargava and John Taggart. The company has raised $78M to date and operates within a well-capitalized sector. Our peer universe comprises 9 private companies and 1 public company (LNZA), with comparable companies including KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Amogy, and Redwood Materials operating at Series C stage or public markets.

We applied two triangulation methods to WeaveGrid's valuation. Stage-progression analysis uses the $78M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-later-stage advancement, yielding $148M. The peer-median method examines three same-sector, adjacent-stage comparables: KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M. This peer set produces a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range of $700M to $3.0B.

The two methods produce meaningfully different results, reflecting the dispersion inherent in early-stage climate tech valuations. Triangulating both approaches yields a low-to-high range of $126M to $1.1B, with a median of $574M. The material gap between stage-progression and peer-median results reflects uncertainty around WeaveGrid's relative technology maturity, market traction, and capital efficiency versus the peer cohort. Critical unknowns include unit economics, customer concentration, and technology differentiation relative to the $700M–$3.0B peer range.
